archive/974-service-home-successor-route.thesis: A shared territorial service home is not proved by a single strong case example; it needs a reusable service map, authority/operator split, local front door, complaint handoff, continuity duty, and source-boundary route.

archive/975-cloudtainer-service-home-red.thesis: A successor service-home route does not retire note 615 unless every protected element is mapped into note 974, generated service-home tests, source keys, and applied examples with visible redirect limits.

archive/976-cloudtainer-reader-visible-s.thesis: A protected-element redirect ledger only reduces route-retirement risk when ordinary readers can see it from the old route, successor route, generated retirement audit, and generated redirect surface.

archive/977-cloudtainer-final-preservati.title: 977 — Cloudtainer final preservation review for service-home route 615: route-residue ledger, status guard, and no retirement by complete redirect path

archive/978-applied-service-home-case-pa.thesis: A homelessness service home is not proved by a joint-powers authority, budget waist, provider network, or dashboard; it requires visible service promises, operator chains, complaint handoffs, payment continuity, and transition receipts.

archive/979-applied-emergency-service-ho.thesis: An emergency communications service home is not proved by an NG911 platform, PSAP map, statewide bridge contract, or FCC reliability rule; it needs visible caller promise, operator chain, GIS/routing seam, outage fallback, complaint/QA route, and continuity duty.
archive/979-applied-emergency-service-ho.title: 979 — Applied emergency service-home case packet for NG911, PSAPs, ESInet, GIS, CAD, outage handoff, and no rescue by platform waist

archive/980-applied-digital-administrati.thesis: A shared government account, proofing service, status page, or connected-service list does not create a digital-administrative service home unless GDS platform duties, relying-service duties, support, fallback, representative access, incident handoff, and migration receipts remain visible.
archive/980-applied-digital-administrati.title: 980 — Applied digital-administrative service-home case packet for GOV.UK One Login, HMRC, DWP, relying services, and no service home by shared account

archive/981-applied-local-digital-servic.thesis: A local digital portal, Common Services layer, business dashboard, benefits redirect, childcare submission row, or chatbot does not create a city service home unless agency ownership, workflow state, support/complaint handoff, data-sharing boundary, vendor chain, fallback, and outcome joins remain visible.
archive/981-applied-local-digital-servic.title: 981 — Applied local digital service-home case packet for NYC MyCity, Common Services, childcare, business, benefits, and no service home by portal

archive/982-cloudtainer-decision-packet-.thesis: A required interoperability assessment record can be part of procedural-digital governance, but it does not preserve the generic decision-packet route for determination classes, reasons, effectivity, implementation duties, review clocks, withdrawal, correction, and supersession.
archive/982-cloudtainer-decision-packet-.title: 982 — Cloudtainer decision-packet merge review for note 720, Interoperable Europe assessment forms, and no decision packet by assessment record

archive/983-cloudtainer-mission-kernel-r.thesis: The archive should prove public outcomes and its own integrity through reproducible artifacts, complete schema coverage, live gaps, compact routes, and affected-person evidence; internal consistency alone is not governance proof.
archive/983-cloudtainer-mission-kernel-r.title: 983 — Cloudtainer mission kernel, reproducible build, schema completeness, route gravity, affected-person proof, and no governance by self-consistent cube

archive/984-cloudtainer-affected-person-.thesis: Affected-person proof must move from mission diagnosis into bounded receipts and operational tests for UI and housing, while source receipts record official-source limits instead of pretending field validation is complete.
archive/984-cloudtainer-affected-person-.title: 984 — Cloudtainer affected-person evidence pilot, UI and housing receipt tests, source-receipt spine, build-registry refactor, and no proof by official surface

archive/985-cloudtainer-closure-gates-fo.thesis: Evidence receipts must carry proof floors and closure blockers so they prevent premature repair claims, while one low-risk route demotion proves preservation can coexist with taking a note out of active circulation.
archive/985-cloudtainer-closure-gates-fo.title: 985 — Cloudtainer closure gates for affected-person proof, evidence-receipt floors, route-demotion pilot, and no closure by receipt row

archive/986-cloudtainer-field-signal-mat.thesis: Aggregate claimant feedback and household outcome surfaces move the archive beyond official guidance, but they still cannot close affected-person, source-preservation, or material-distribution gaps without privacy-bounded person or household tails.
archive/986-cloudtainer-field-signal-mat.title: 986 — Cloudtainer field signal, material outcome floor, source-receipt triage, taxonomy pressure, and no closure by aggregate

archive/987-cloudtainer-claim-passage-re.thesis: Source keys and field signals now need claim-passage locators and privacy-bounded outcome-tail plans before they can support closure; URLs, aggregates, and sampling plans remain blockers, not repairs.
archive/987-cloudtainer-claim-passage-re.title: 987 — Cloudtainer claim-passage receipts, outcome-tail plans, source-health taxonomy-alias refactor, and no source by URL

archive/988-cloudtainer-tail-sampling-ga.thesis: Outcome-tail plans now require sampling-frame, nonresponse-bias, privacy, and source-preservation gates before any affected-person or material-outcome gap can move toward closure.
archive/988-cloudtainer-tail-sampling-ga.title: 988 — Cloudtainer tail-sampling gates, nonresponse-bias floors, preservation controls, metadata-surface refactor, and no closure by sampling plan

archive/989-cloudtainer-field-intake-con.thesis: Sampling gates still cannot authorize contacting claimants or households; rev0791 adds pre-collection intake, consent/lawful-basis, PII-separation, linkage-key, adverse-action, and publication firewalls before any field-tail evidence can be collected.
archive/989-cloudtainer-field-intake-con.title: 989 — Cloudtainer field-intake controls, consent/linkage firewalls, source-preservation safeguards, and no fieldwork by gate

archive/990-cloudtainer-fieldwork-author.thesis: Field-intake controls still cannot authorize contact, record linkage, or private-data custody; rev0792 adds non-closing authorization and custody handoff gates so fieldwork cannot begin without named owners, legal/privacy/ethics review, secure environment, disclosure review, and stop conditions outside the cube.
archive/990-cloudtainer-fieldwork-author.title: 990 — Cloudtainer fieldwork authorization gates, data-custody handoffs, oversight receipts, and no collection by control

archive/991-cloudtainer-fieldwork-execut.thesis: Authorization gates still do not produce safe evidence; rev0793 adds non-closing execution controls for pause clocks, adverse-event and incident reporting, PII breach response, audit-log failure, retention/destruction authority, and disclosure-reviewed release so operating logs cannot be mistaken for claimant or household outcomes.
archive/991-cloudtainer-fieldwork-execut.title: 991 — Cloudtainer fieldwork execution controls, incident clocks, audit logs, retention/release, and no outcome by operating log

archive/992-cloudtainer-fieldwork-releas.thesis: A disclosure-reviewed public output can become useful evidence only after release controls pass, but it still cannot prove claimant or household outcomes by itself; rev0794 adds non-closing release controls after execution controls.
archive/992-cloudtainer-fieldwork-releas.title: 992 — Cloudtainer fieldwork release controls, disclosure limitation, public-output audit, and no outcome by release packet

archive/993-cloudtainer-fieldwork-correc.thesis: A correction, erratum, withdrawal, or republication can repair a public artifact but cannot prove claimant or household outcomes; rev0795 adds non-closing post-release correction controls after release controls.
archive/993-cloudtainer-fieldwork-correc.title: 993 — Cloudtainer fieldwork correction controls, errata/withdrawal/redress ledgers, and no outcome by corrigendum

archive/994-cloudtainer-redress-verifica.thesis: A redress route, correction ticket, or follow-up ledger can show that repair work was assigned, but not that claimants or households were actually made whole; rev0796 adds non-closing redress-verification controls after correction controls.
archive/994-cloudtainer-redress-verifica.title: 994 — Cloudtainer redress verification controls, follow-through ledgers, internal-control repair, and no outcome by redress route

archive/995-cloudtainer-closure-dossiers.title: 995 — Cloudtainer closure dossiers, attestation matrix, gap reopen triggers, and no outcome by attestation
archive/995-cloudtainer-closure-dossiers.thesis: A closure dossier, owner attestation, or independent review statement can make future gap closure reviewable, but it cannot prove claimant or household outcomes; rev0797 adds non-ready closure-dossier controls after redress verification.

archive/996-cloudtainer-post-closure-mon.title: 996 — Cloudtainer post-closure monitoring, reopen clocks, drift guards, and no closure forever
archive/996-cloudtainer-post-closure-mon.thesis: A closure dossier can make a future closure decision reviewable, but closure is not permanent finality; rev0798 adds post-closure monitoring controls so recurrence, source decay, denominator drift, and later affected-person evidence can qualify or reopen gaps.
